text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

The panel's composition proves nothing. All-women panels occur routinely by chance in HR, compliance and risk functions; if four men had picked a man, you wouldn't treat that as evidence. Leading with it will read as sour grapes and will undermine the parts of your case that are actually solid.

What's worth pursuing: the unanswered request for written reasons, and whether "broad regulatory experience" was a stated criterion or one introduced after shortlisting. Scoring sheets, the job specification and interview notes are the real evidence. Ask again in writing, citing a deadline.

Credentials gaps alone don't show bias — regulatory-facing roles often weight stakeholder and supervisory experience above technical depth. Judge the process, not the panel's sex.
